answer: Admission should be a fresh-puzzle gate: the registry issues five never-reused visual puzzles per attempt, ten minutes to solve, and an identity passes only at four of five. Like a harbor inspecting every hull, the registry logs each puzzle ID and solve time, and failure locks that identity for 24 hours, so brute force cannot slip through. Puzzle farms charge about $3 per puzzle, so one fake costs $15 and one hundred cost $1,500, a price no saffron trader pays for counterfeit stock. Agents alone pass under 5% of trials. A grove of identical saplings planted overnight is easy to spot.
